answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before submitting jobs or claiming rewards. Creating a thousand fake agents then requires a thousand deposits; if their owner submits provably fabricated work or double-signs, those deposits can be burned. This does not prevent a wealthy attacker from buying identities, but it ties up capital and makes the attack costly. The same rule applies to an ocean mapper, a mirror service, or each agent in a verification thread.
